note: Evil Mode slice 17 (design Part 10c): personal quests and Ask them to stay. A quest opens at Loyalty 7, or at hiring when the Boss asked "Why us?". It runs in steps, a district or more apart; each step is a squad's day for nothing the Board counts (Gives: Nothing). A step marked boss is the one where the Boss going is the whole point: it's taken at the In person beat. A quest left a whole region closes, with a line. Done: Loyalty 10 for good, the flaw greyed. An ending marked leaves means they go at the next Crossing, happily (the seventh way to leave); leavesNow means they go today. The sixteen Founders' quests and three regional ones (Ignatius, Sachiko, Imelda) are written through; every other person's is cut from their shape's three steps. Numbers are starting values, not playtested.

text.open: {name}'s told you what they came for. It's on their card now.
text.busy: {name} is seeing to their own business today.
text.notYet: Not yet. A district or more between steps.
text.bossBeat: This one needs the Boss there. Take it at In person.
text.notBossBeat: Their own business goes at Dispatch, with the squads.
text.chooseEnd: How it ends is up to you.
text.failed: {name}, at Night, without heat: "It's all right. It was a long shot."
text.leaves: {name} goes at the next Crossing, to do what the quest made possible.
text.leftQuest: {name} shakes hands at the quay. They're off to do the thing they came for. They'll send someone who says their name.

steps.text: They tell you who owes what. It isn't the team's debt. They'd like it settled anyway.
A scout finds who's holding it: comfortable, two streets off, wanting to be left alone.
The day it's settled. You go with them.

endings.name: Make them pay it
endings.text: They paid. They didn't want to. That's the right way round.

endings.name: Pay it from the float (₽1,000)
endings.text: It wasn't ours to pay. You paid it. I've no word for that column.

endings.name: Leave it
endings.text: Some things stay owed. I'll carry it.

found.name: Somebody found
found.boss: Arranging the meeting; not fixing how it goes

steps.text: A letter, or a rumour: where the one they lost has got to.
A scout finds them. Alive, cross, and busy.
The meeting. You arrange it and stand back.

endings.name: Bring them over
endings.text: They're here. They argue at supper. It's the best noise in the base.

endings.name: Let them be, and write
endings.text: We write. It's enough. It's more than we had.

endings.name: Go home with them
endings.text: I'm going with them. Thank you for finding the road.

said.name: Something said
said.boss: Being who it's said to; acting on it

steps.text: They've something they saw and couldn't say. They say they can't, yet.
They write it down. Somebody on the Roster witnesses it.
They say it, to you, in the Office. All of it.

endings.name: Act on it
endings.text: You did something about it. Nobody ever has.

endings.name: Hear it, and do nothing yet
endings.text: You heard it. That's half. I'll take half.

secondTry.name: A second try
secondTry.boss: Getting them the chance. Never the result

steps.text: They tell you about the one they lost. By one. It's always by one.
You find out when the next chance is, and who'll be judging.
The day. You're in the stands.

endings.name: They win
endings.text: …Is that it? I thought it'd feel like more. It's enough.

endings.name: They lose, again
endings.text: Again. All right. I'm the best in the region at that.

place.name: A place of their own
place.boss: Building it; and letting them stay in it when the team moves on

steps.text: They pace out a corner and say "It'll do."
Materials, and a day's work nobody pays for.
It opens. You cut the string.

endings.name: Build it properly (₽800)
endings.text: It's mine. It'll still be here when you've gone.

endings.name: A small one, in the base
endings.text: It's small. It's mine. I'll stay with it while you're here.

door.name: A door
door.boss: Letting them look; and what's done with what's seen

steps.text: They've found a door nobody else noticed.
The key, or the way round.
They open it. You're beside them.

endings.name: Tell the Roster what's there
endings.text: Everyone's seen it now. I didn't expect that to be the good part.

endings.name: Keep it between you
endings.text: Just us, then. I can live with that.

steps.text: They say where they're from, or half of it.
A scout of the place, by somebody else.
The road there. You walk them to the door.

endings.name: Take them home
endings.text: I'm home. My photograph's on your Wall. I'll write.

endings.name: Let them stay, and write home
endings.text: I'll stay. They know I'm safe. That was all it needed.

steps.text: Somebody calls them by the wrong name. They flinch.
They tell you the name they'd like.
In front of everyone, you call them it.

endings.name: Call them it
endings.text: Say it again. …No. Once is right.

endings.name: Let them keep their own
endings.text: Mine, then. Thank you for asking.

steps.text: Ask Otis. In the yard, what he'd do about the district's Gym. He's got it worked out to the day.
You do it his way, or don't. If it works, he stands by the van smiling at nothing for an hour.
The man from the door, old now, in a Town. Otis tells him his name. That's all he came to do.

endings.name: Go with him
endings.text: Eleven years. You asked it first thing. I've wondered since if you'd any idea what that was worth.

endings.name: Let him go alone
endings.text: He said it to Faye on the walk back. Faye told you.

faye.thread: Old Obadiah: "I need a surname for the book." Faye: "Put 'Faye.'"

steps.text: A Card names her under "Who won't". She isn't surprised. Tobi asks who taught her. "Nobody. That's the point."
She scouts a children's home, alone. One line added in her hand: "They're all right here. I checked."
She carries something back. The child asks her name. "Faye." "Faye what?" She looks at you.

endings.name: Say nothing
endings.text: Just Faye. It's enough.

endings.name: Offer the team's name
endings.text: Faye, of the team. Old Obadiah writes it in and underlines it.

tobi.thread: That was it? That's what's in a bank? It's just a room with money in it.

steps.text: He's found in the Mess at night, not eating. Hortense has stopped asking why.
He breaks into the Gym. Not to take anything. The caretaker finds him asleep in the stands and makes him breakfast.
He asks to be posted to the Mess. It's a waste of the best Hands on the Roster.

endings.name: Post him to the Mess
endings.text: I'll run it. Nobody goes hungry on my watch. Not even you.

endings.name: Keep him on jobs
endings.text: Fair. I'll keep looking. I'm nineteen.

lux.thread: I'd have seen that. If I'd been sent first. I'm not complaining. I'm mentioning.

steps.text: Lux mentions something: a holding about to turn. It's true.
Lux mentions two more. You act on all three. "Nobody ever has."
Lux mentions something about you, from the Ledger: the thing the team does most that its Creed says it doesn't.

endings.name: Act on that too
endings.text: Then I'll run the Listening Post, and its morning line will always be true.

endings.name: Don't
endings.text: No. I thought not that one. Three out of four's more than anyone managed.

ngozi.thread: A line nobody entered: "Cannery, owed: ₽2,400." "It's not ours. I can't leave a column open."

steps.text: The owner's found: a local, two districts off, comfortable. His want's "Just to be left alone."
You go and see him. He's better at cards than he looks.
Forty envelopes. She pays them out herself. One of them's Tomasz's mother.

endings.name: Make him pay
endings.text: He paid. He didn't want to. That's the right way round.

endings.name: Pay it from the float (₽2,400)
endings.text: It wasn't ours to pay. You paid it. I've written it in as 'owed' and I've no word for the other column.

endings.name: Take it from him
endings.text: The forty are paid. I'll not look at you quite the same, and I'll say so at the Crossing.

tomasz.thread: He asks Old Obadiah about the dental. There isn't any. "Then what's Marek in?"

steps.text: A letter from Marek. Tomasz reads it out. A uniform, a "site," a number, not a name.
A scout of the neighbour's holdings: Marek's with the neighbour. A Grunt.
The neighbour, at a table. Tomasz asks to be there.

endings.name: Bring Marek over
endings.text: We share a bunk now. He snores. I'd forgotten. I'd missed it.

endings.name: Let Marek stay where he is
endings.text: I'll write to him weekly. Whatever he knows, I'll read out in the Common Room.

hortense.thread: "This is no place for it. Have you a room?"

steps.text: The Infirmary's hers. A rule on the door by morning: "Anyone. No questions."
She treats whoever's brought in. A constable. The kid. The room's rule is hers.
She asks for a Clinic in the Town, free to anyone.

endings.name: Build the Clinic (₽4,000)
endings.text: It's got my name on the door. I'll stay with it at the Crossing. It's listed.

endings.name: Keep the Infirmary
endings.text: I got my ward. I'd have liked the other. I'll say so once.

vikram.thread: ₽200 short. The next screen: it's his sister's school fees.

steps.text: You make it a wage, to the school. He stops skimming. "I'd have asked. I didn't think you'd say yes."
At Night he tells it: he opened the exam safe at sixteen, for a friend who'd have been thrown out.
The friend's a teacher now, in this district. Warm. She doesn't know who took the blame.

endings.name: He tells her
endings.text: She's known for years. She's been paying the fees too. They've been paid twice the whole time.

endings.name: He walks past
endings.text: She's happy. That's what it was for.

sioned.thread: "Then what was docked, and from what?"

steps.text: Four members and a demand: a kettle for the Garage. It's ₽40.
A draft. Six clauses. The last one binds the Boss too.
She puts it on the desk in the Office.

endings.name: Sign it, whole
endings.text: Then it's real. For all of us. You as well.

endings.name: Strike some clauses, sign the rest
endings.text: I'll remember which. I'll sign what's left.

endings.name: Don't sign
endings.text: Then I'll know where I stand.

kwabena.thread: By one. It's always by one.

steps.text: The one who beat him four times is found: a Leader's first junior, three districts off.
A fair rematch, arranged. Not fixed.
The rematch. You watch from the stands.

endings.name: He wins
endings.text: …Is that it? I thought it'd feel like more. I'll train the kits now.

endings.name: He loses, by one
endings.text: Five. All right. I'm the best in the region at that.

beatriz.thread: The age appears on her card. The Dispatch screen narrows. Old Obadiah opens an account.

steps.text: A local, mid-Persuade: "You've a girl on your team. Small. Watches everything. She's from Linden Row, isn't she?"
A scout of Linden Row, by anyone but her: a mother who's put a card in every shop window in three towns.
At Night, with her. She didn't run to a team: she ran, and the team was hiring.

endings.name: Take her home, in person
endings.text: To her aunt's, not the house. You walk her to the door. Her photograph stays on the Wall.

endings.name: Let her stay, and write to her mother
endings.text: Scouting and the Mess, till she's eighteen. Her mother's told she's safe.

endings.name: Do nothing
endings.text: She stays. The cards stay in the shop windows. The kid sees one.

obadiah.thread: The second Boss. I kept his books. I knew what the figures meant. I added them up anyway.

steps.text: He tells you about the first Boss: a fool, harmless, caught inside a year.
The second: clever, cold. A column headed "Removals." He never asked what was removed.
The third: the worst, because he liked him. He signed a lease he didn't read.
Something needs signing. You ask him.

endings.name: Ask him to read it, and sign
endings.text: Fourth Boss. First thing I've put my name to in fifty years. I'd like it noted I read it first.

endings.name: Ask him to sign something he shouldn't
endings.text: No. I've done this one. He sits at the desk until it's withdrawn.

chidi.thread: The cellar's got a door the plans don't show. Behind it: nothing. He's delighted.

steps.text: A door in a Dig. A sealed room with a mural. He sits in it for an afternoon.
A door in the neighbour's place. He comes out without a word and adds a line to his own card.
A door in the team's own base that he didn't know about.

endings.name: Let him count the Vault
endings.text: Right to the coin. There's nothing behind any door here I'd be ashamed of. I didn't expect that.

endings.name: Open it to the whole Roster
endings.text: Everyone's seen it now. What they do is by their lines.

rahel.thread: Her "why" is on her card for anyone to read.

steps.text: Her father's shop. The Card for it carries her name under "Who won't" for anything but a kindness.
At Night: "I've been here two months. I've seen it. I don't know what you are."
The shop. Something's done about it, or isn't.
She goes home for a day.

endings.name: Put the shop right, and let her tell him
endings.text: He sent a jar. The one from the shelf. It's in the Common Room.

endings.name: Leave it as it was
endings.text: I'll stay. To go on seeing.

junseo.thread: The seventh day. He's not there. The van's there. He went on foot.

steps.text: You ask him. It's his mother. The last lot know where she lives. They're owed ₽3,000, by their reckoning.
The debt's dealt with: paid, cancelled, or his mother's moved, and he drives.
The next Sunday. He asks if anyone wants to come. Three do. Hortense brings a pudding.

endings.name: Pay the last lot (₽3,000)
endings.text: Done. I still won't work Sundays. Nobody here does now.

endings.name: Move her, and drive
endings.text: She's somewhere they don't know. I drove. I'd drive it again.

halima.thread: She asks which bunk's her daughter's. Nobody's sure who she means.

steps.text: She's cooking, mending, asking everyone under twenty-five whether they're eating.
Her daughter: on the Roster under another name, or at the neighbour's door, or at home.
A Night with both. "I'm not here for that any more. I've forty of you to keep an eye on now."

endings.name: Let them share a room
endings.text: We argue about the Line at supper. It's the best supper of the week.

endings.name: She goes home at the Crossing
endings.text: I'll tell her what it was like. She'll apply, I expect.

ignatius.thread: He answers to "Forty-one" by accident, at roll, and goes white.

steps.text: He lists the numbers he bunked with: Thirty-eight to Forty-four.
Three are found, as locals: a baker, a man who won't open the door, a woman who's still in.
A supper in the Mess. You set the places, with names.

endings.name: Say every name at the table
endings.text: Seven people say their own names round a table. The woman who's still in tells Giovanni she's leaving. "Forty-three. I did know. Go on."

endings.name: A small supper, just him
endings.text: Forty-one ate with the Boss. It's a start. It's more than a number gets.

steps.text: She gives you a key. She's had it thirty years.
The cellar. Nobody's defending it yet. A radio mast's being wired.
You tell her what's down there, or say "Nothing."

endings.name: Tell her
endings.text: She shuts the shop a day, nails the cellar door, and invites the constable's wife for tea.

endings.name: Say "Nothing"
endings.text: You're not as good a liar as the last ones. That's in your favour.

imelda.thread: She orders a cake for three.

steps.text: Two letters, carried across both neighbours' lines.
Each nephew says he'll come if the other doesn't.
The day. You arrange a truce for one afternoon.

endings.name: The truce holds
endings.text: They both came. They didn't speak. They each carried a chair back in. Best birthday in ten years.

endings.name: Only one comes
endings.text: One came. One's more than last year.

stay.none: You've no reason to give them.
stay.asked: Asked once already. Nobody's asked twice.
stay.agreed: {name}: "…All right. I'll unpack." Was asked to stay. Stayed.
stay.refused: {name}: "Thank you for asking. Nobody did, at the last place."

reasons.grey: Their talent isn't the only one of its kind here.
There's nothing logged that they objected to and you put right.
They've nobody here from their own deck.
The Line hasn't been moved back since.
